title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap scheduler improvements
author: Aditi Menon
description:
Motivation:
High-percentile latency and overall GPU utilization on mixed prefill/decode workloads show inefficiencies related to how prefill is currently handled: large prefill batches block decode scheduling and the kernel scheduler frequently under-utilizes available SMs when sequence lengths and KV cache hits vary. This PR introduces two complementary improvements: 1) chunked speculative prefill: break long prefill requests into smaller speculative chunks that can be prefetched and later committed to the KV cache to reduce tail latency and improve overlap with decodes; 2) stage-overlap-aware kernel scheduler: extend the scheduler to be aware of prefill/decode stage transitions and preferentially schedule decode-ready work to reduce blocking.

Summary of changes:
- Implement chunked speculative prefill in runtime/pipeline/prefill.py and C++ execution path to support progressive KV writeback and speculative token generation.
- Add a stage-overlap hint to the kernel scheduler (runtime/scheduler/kernel_scheduler.cpp) so that decode micro-batches are prioritized when upstream prefill chunks are still streaming.
- KV cache manager updates to support chunk commit/rollback semantics (runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.cpp).
- Perf tests and canary benchmark updates, new perf test harness for mixed prefill/decode scenarios (tests/perf/test_prefill_throughput.py, benchmarks/prefill_decode_throughput.md).
- Config knobs exposed via runtime configs: prefill.chunk_size, prefill.speculative_enabled, scheduler.stage_overlap_threshold.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for new scheduler hints and chunk commit logic
- [x] Integration perf test demonstrating >18% p99 improvement for mixed workloads
- [x] Backwards compatible default behavior (speculative prefill disabled by default)
- [x] Documentation note in release notes and runtime config reference

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-3412, ENG-3490.

Notes on behavior and opt-in:
- Speculative chunking is opt-in via prefill.speculative_enabled; default is false to avoid behavioral changes for conservative customers.
- When enabled, chunked prefill will attempt to speculatively execute chunks and write temporary KV entries. If the prefill later diverges (e.g. due to caching or reroutes) we roll back temporary entries.
- The kernel scheduler uses a conservative heuristic (scheduler.stage_overlap_threshold) to avoid starvation of long prefill-heavy workloads while still prioritizing latency-sensitive decode micro-batches.

Benchmark summary (see tests/perf for details):
- Mixed workload (30% prefill by tokens, 70% decode interactive): p99 latency down 18.4%, average GPU token throughput up 9.2% under default canary hardware (A100 80GB).
- Pure prefill throughput unchanged within noise when speculative disabled; small 2-4% improvement when speculative is enabled due to better batching opportunities.

Migration: no forced migrations. New config options documented in runtime reference.
